title: Graph Attention Networks
layout_note: Two panels. Left: the attention mechanism as a small neural diagram - eight input units bracketed as W h_i and W h_j feed one LeakyReLU unit via weight vector a, then a softmax_j arrow up to alpha_ij. Right: node h1 in the centre with five neighbours h2-h6 around it and a self-loop; each spoke carries three arrows (one per head) labelled alpha_1j, and thick translucent arrows labelled concat/avg exit to h1' on the right.
grouping: No frames or tints; the two panels are separated by whitespace. Under the left panel two curly braces group the input units into W h_i and W h_j. In the right panel the three attention heads are grouped by colour and line style (blue straight, green zigzag, purple wavy).
shapes_depth: Flat black-and-white line art: all nodes are white circles with black outlines and math labels; the activation unit has a drawn LeakyReLU glyph inside; head arrows are thin coloured lines, the output arrows thick and semi-transparent.
proposed_highlight: Colour is used only for the three attention heads in the right panel; the left panel is uncoloured line art, so the multi-head neighbourhood aggregation is the visual focus.
lesson: Show multi-head attention on a graph as one hub node with neighbour spokes, each spoke carrying one parallel arrow per head in a distinct colour and line style, merging into one output arrow.
notes: Venue from the first page ('Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2018').

arrangement.units: two unframed panels side by side on whitespace: the attention-coefficient computation (left) and the multi-head neighbourhood aggregation around one node (right)
arrangement.inputs_as: left: a row of eight small unit circles under two curly braces W h_i and W h_j; right: neighbour feature nodes h2-h6 ringed around the centre node
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the figure shows the layer computation only
arrangement.shared: the attention mechanism of the left panel is not redrawn on the right; its output appears as alpha labels on each spoke

taxonomy.task: node classification with attention-weighted neighbourhood aggregation

insights.structure: A narrow left panel (input units -> activation unit -> alpha_ij, stacked vertically) sits beside a wide right panel where the hub node h1 is ringed by five neighbours with an output node h1' off to the right.
insights.data: Every quantity is a white circle with a math label (h-vector, alpha_ij, h1'); feature vectors on the left are rows of tiny unit circles under curly braces, and attention weights are spoke labels rather than drawn values.
insights.emphasis: The three heads are the only coloured elements, each with its own line style, so multi-head attention stands out against the otherwise black line art.
insights.flow: Left panel reads bottom-to-top along converging arrows; right panel reads radially inward along the spokes to h1, then left-to-right along the thick concat/avg arrow to h1'.
insights.avoid: The head encoding (blue straight, green zigzag, purple wavy) has no key in the figure, and three parallel lines per spoke plus rotated alpha labels make the hub crowded.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
